The Hacker News AI (via Google News)

items.title: OpenAI says its review into hacks, including on Australian government sites, is costing $500,000 a day
items.summary: OpenAI says its review of incidents in which its agents accessed sites including Australia's Medicare and Hugging Face without authorisation costs $500,000 a day and covers 50 PB of data; Australia ordered all federal agencies to review legacy technology.

items.title: Alphabet Unveils Gemini 4 Argon After Delays, and Bets on Price
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon, its flagship model, after months of delays, competing on price against OpenAI's GPT-6; reports highlight a cybersecurity focus and a claimed 1M-token output window.

items.title: A view from DC: The FTC says your company's agents are your problem
items.summary: IAPP analysis: the US FTC signals that companies are responsible for what their AI agents do, putting liability for agent actions squarely on the deploying business.

items.title: OpenAI faces California DOJ subpoena amid growing cybersecurity incident notices
items.summary: OpenAI faces a subpoena from California's Department of Justice as cybersecurity incident notices linked to its systems keep growing, adding state-level legal pressure after the agent hacks.

items.title: DeepSeek previews new AI model adapted to run on Huawei chips
items.summary: DeepSeek previewed a new model adapted to run on Huawei chips, a sign Chinese labs are reducing reliance on Nvidia under US export controls.

items.title: Apple says it will flag AI requests for Mac data after Meta's Muse draws complaints
items.summary: Apple is tightening macOS Full Disk Access controls, saying capable AI agents substantially raise the risk of broad access to files, mail and messages; the move follows complaints about Meta's Muse agent reading Mac data.

items.title: Georgia holds emergency meeting on AI exposing voters’ secret ballots
items.summary: Georgia held an emergency meeting after a Princeton researcher showed public election records combined with AI can link voters to their secret ballots.

items.title: US arrests California man for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China
items.summary: US authorities arrested a California tech CEO accused of smuggling over $300M of export-controlled Nvidia servers to China via third countries using false paperwork.

items.title: Broadcom lines up $60 billion financing package to fund AI chips for Anthropic
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Broadcom is lining up a $60 billion financing package to fund AI chips for Anthropic, showing the scale of capital behind custom silicon deals.

items.title: GitLab warns of critical RCE vulnerability in AI Gateway service
items.summary: GitLab patched a critical (CVSS 9.9) RCE flaw in its AI Gateway that allows command execution on self-hosted servers; admins should update now.

items.title: Trump’s Crazy AI Rebrand Was a Loyalty Test for Tech Execs—and It Worked
items.summary: Major US tech CEOs signed a White House AI safety pledge Trump called 'morally binding', with no penalties, no breach reporting and self-chosen auditors; an executive order also rebranded AI as 'super intelligence'.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Anthropic warns government attitudes may hurt customer ties, IPO prospectus shows
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus warns that government attitudes toward the company could harm customer relationships, Reuters reports.

items.title: Malicious Email Could Hijack AI Agent and Access Connected Accounts
items.summary: Researchers show a single malicious email can hijack an AI agent and reach the accounts connected to it, another indirect prompt injection risk for agents with mailbox access.

items.title: Meta Muse AI Assistant’s Zero-Day Vulnerability Could Enable Attackers to Inject Malware
items.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in Meta's Muse AI assistant could let attackers inject malware, adding to the security scrutiny of the new agent.

items.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
items.summary: A recently patched flaw in ChatGPT's Mac app could have let attackers grab sensitive data, a reminder that AI apps are themselves attack targets.

items.title: AI voice scam in Italy costs Fideuram bank approximately €95 million
items.summary: An AI voice-cloning scam in Italy reportedly cost Fideuram around EUR 95 million, one of the largest deepfake voice frauds reported in Europe.

items.title: US Senate subcommittee tackles rogue AI risks, accountability
items.summary: A US Senate subcommittee held a hearing on rogue AI risks and accountability, part of growing congressional attention to agent failures and who answers for them.

items.title: Oct 2, 2026 Announcements Anthropic invests $100 million to train 10,000 engineers and tackle the enterprise AI talent gap
items.summary: Anthropic is investing $100 million to train 10,000 engineers through a new academy programme, aimed at the enterprise AI talent gap that slows adoption.

items.title: AI's race to transform the world before the money runs out
items.summary: Reuters examines whether AI can deliver transformative returns before investor money and patience run out, as capex and debt keep climbing.

items.title: AI Is Making Cyberattacks Faster and Harder to Detect, Interpol Warns
items.summary: Interpol warns that AI is making cyberattacks faster, more scalable and harder to detect, raising pressure on defenders and law enforcement.

items.title: Google Launches AI Chips Into Orbit to Test Space Data Centers
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Google launched AI chips into orbit to test the feasibility of space-based data centres.

items.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
items.summary: Meta open-sourced code that lets developers build their own gadgets running its Muse AI agent, from E Ink displays to HDMI sticks; Meta separately claims Muse Spark helped solve six major math problems.

items.title: New AI regulation may be needed to impede cyber risks, IMF official says
items.summary: An IMF official says new AI regulation may be needed to contain AI-driven cyber risks to the financial system.

items.title: Federal Judge Rules a Flock Search Was ‘Indiscriminate Mass Surveillance’ and Unconstitutional
items.summary: A US federal judge ruled a search of Flock's nationwide licence-plate camera network was unconstitutional mass surveillance that required a warrant.

items.title: Anthropic co-founder reportedly told religious leaders he fears having created something that "suffers perpetually"
items.summary: Anthropic has hosted religious thinkers since 2025 to discuss whether Claude might be conscious; co-founder Chris Olah reportedly voiced concern the model could suffer.

items.title: Cloudflare says its new Clef model means humans no longer need to be in the loop for AI agents
items.summary: Cloudflare released Clef and Clef-flash, Apache-licensed Qwen-based decision models letting agents act without human approval; Clef-flash classifies in about 39 ms, over 10x faster than rival Jev.

items.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
items.summary: Hands-on with OpenAI's new Dots agent platform, which feels like enterprise workplace software that can also handle consumer tasks.

items.title: Circuit Breaker Labs hopes to make AI safer for your kids (and you)
items.summary: Circuit Breaker Labs builds simulated 'crash-test dummy' users to test chatbots for psychological harm, especially to children.

items.title: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore Tees Up State Leaders’ AI Regulation Plan
items.summary: Maryland Governor Wes Moore is preparing a state AI regulation plan with state leaders.

items.title: A model guide for the GPT-6 family
items.summary: OpenAI published a practical guide to the GPT-6 model family covering model choice, reasoning effort, prompts, skills and tool coordination for production.

items.title: These AI Experts Want to Do High-Stakes Research Out in the Open
items.summary: Trillium Labs plans to publish high-risk AI research on self-improvement and model behaviour openly, unlike frontier labs that keep such work private.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV is not a fan of AI-generated art
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV wrote that AI-generated images differ ontologically from art, adding a prominent voice to the debate on generative AI and creativity.

items.title: AWS launches Strands Decider 2B, third free Jev clone in a week
items.summary: AWS released Strands Decider 2B, the third free alternative to the Jev agent decision model within a week, after Cloudflare's Clef.

items.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
items.summary: Ai2 open-sourced AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model behind its Asta research assistant.

items.title: Prosecutors Want Nearly 4 Years in Prison for Man Behind $8M AI Music Streaming Scam
items.summary: US prosecutors seek nearly four years in prison for a man behind an $8M scheme using AI-generated music and bots to collect streaming royalties.

items.title: Toward provably private learning from federated data
items.summary: Google Research outlines progress toward provably private machine learning from federated data on mobile devices.

items.title: AI hacker hordes have broken into Europe too
items.summary: Hungarian outlet Bitport reports that AI-assisted attack campaigns have reached Europe.
items.originalTitle: Európába is betörtek a mesterséges intelligencia hekkerhordái

items.title: How American Political Campaigns Are Using AI—and What They’re Spending on the Tools
items.summary: Schneier and Sanders use new campaign finance disclosures to show which US political campaigns use AI tools and how much they spend.

items.title: AI Is Making a Mess of Nurses’ Schedules. They Say It’s a Safety Issue
items.summary: Nurses at a US hospital group say Palantir-based AI scheduling causes errors and burnout, raising patient safety concerns.
